name: Hauna Trade Language
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ronald K. Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 243-273. Canberra: ANU. Handle 1885/253564
sources.note: Nothing on stress (0 hits for stress/accent). Only sociolinguistic mention of the pidgin: p. 247-248 'The adult Pai male speakers know a trade language named Yahapiri by means of which they communicate with Walio speakers and also the Sepik Iwam speakers at Hauna. The younger generation knows Yahapiri to a very limited extent, and we predict it will die out...'; p. 253 '...a trade language called Yahipiri, which is known by most of the adult men in Walio, Pai, and some of the Sepik Iwam men from Hauna.'
